**Alexander Victor Schauffele** ([/ˈzændər ˈʃaʊfəleɪ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); born October 25, 1993) is an American [professional golfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_golfer "Professional golfer") who plays on the [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour"). He won the [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship") in 2017 and the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal") at the [men's individual golf event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_individual "Golf at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's individual") of the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Golf at the 2020 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan. He has won two [major championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_major_golf_championships "Men's major golf championships"), both in the same year, the [2024 PGA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_PGA_Championship "2024 PGA Championship") and the [2024 Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Open_Championship "2024 Open Championship"). Schauffele also competed at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-Paris_2024-2)
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Schauffele was born on October 25, 1993, in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-4) to Chen Ping-Yi and Stefan Schauffele.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-5) His mother was born in [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), but grew up in Japan before moving to the United States.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-6) His father Stefan was born in [Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart "Stuttgart") to a French-Austrian mother and a German father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-7) Stefan was an aspiring [decathlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decathlete "Decathlete"). While traveling to the German national training center at age 20, he was hit by a drunk driver and suffered career-ending injuries.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-9) During recovery, he became interested in golf, and later moved to the United States. He worked at a golf academy in San Diego and as an assistant golf professional in Hawaii.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:2-10)
Schauffele's parents met at San Diego's [United States International University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_International_University "United States International University") in 1988 and married three months afterwards.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:0-11) They then moved to Germany, where Xander's elder brother Nico was born, before returning to San Diego.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-12)
Schauffele's father introduced him to golf at age nine, and they joined Bernardo Heights Country Club.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:0-11) Stefan was Xander's only swing coach from that point[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-13) until Xander was aged 30.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:1-14) Stefan's teaching philosophy relies heavily on basic ball flight laws and golf club mechanics. As a result, Xander did not see his own swing until about age 18.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-15) Schauffele began working with [Chris Como](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Como "Chris Como"), formerly a coach of [Tiger Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Woods "Tiger Woods") and [Bryson DeChambeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryson_DeChambeau "Bryson DeChambeau"), in November 2023.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:1-14)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-16)
Two of Schauffele's great-grandfathers played soccer in Europe. [Johann Hoffmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Hoffmann_\(footballer\) "Johann Hoffmann \(footballer\)") played for the [Austria national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_national_football_team "Austria national football team") and won multiple Austrian, Bohemian, and French national titles. After playing football for [VfB Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VfB_Stuttgart "VfB Stuttgart"), [Richard Schauffele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Schauffele "Richard Schauffele") excelled in [track and field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field "Track and field"), garnering over 40 titles in [discus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discus "Discus"), [javelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javelin "Javelin") and [shot put](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shot_put "Shot put").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:2-10) Xander himself played soccer in his youth before focusing on golf,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-17) after his soccer coach refused to reposition him from a defensive midfielder to offensive midfielder.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:2-10)
## Amateur career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Amateur career")]
Schauffele was the individual winner of the 2011 California State High School Championship ([California Interscholastic Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Interscholastic_Federation "California Interscholastic Federation"), CIF), playing for [Scripps Ranch High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scripps_Ranch_High_School "Scripps Ranch High School").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-18) After graduating from high school, Schauffele played his freshman year in college at [California State University Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University_Long_Beach "California State University Long Beach"), where he garnered the 2012 [Big West Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_West_Conference "Big West Conference") Freshman of the Year as well as the 2012 First Team All-Big West awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-lbsu-19)
Prior to his sophomore year, Schauffele transferred to [San Diego State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_State_University "San Diego State University") (SDSU), where eventually he would play out his college career and graduate in 2015. During his three years at SDSU, Schauffele was a Ping and Golfweek Third Team All-American. Scholastically, he was twice awarded the Mountain West Conference All-Academic Team Award. At SDSU, he holds the records for all-time lowest tournament score against par (−17); all-time career scoring average (71.50); as well as the seasonal records for par-5 performance (4.5135); birdies (171) and eagles (9).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-sdsu_record-20)
Schauffele defeated [Beau Hossler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau_Hossler "Beau Hossler") to win the 2014 [California State Amateur Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_Amateur_Championship "California State Amateur Championship") at [La Costa Resort and Spa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Costa_Resort_and_Spa "La Costa Resort and Spa"). Later that summer, the two long-time rivals met again in a final at Chicago's [Beverly Country Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Country_Club "Beverly Country Club") for the 2014 [Western Amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Amateur "Western Amateur"), where Schauffele lost to Hossler in the final match in dramatic fashion.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-21)
Schauffele accumulated a collegiate record that featured 27 top-10s, 19 of which were top-fives, with four of these being runners-up and three wins (from a total of 50 tournaments). He was ranked in the top 10 of the [World Amateur Golf Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Amateur_Golf_Ranking "World Amateur Golf Ranking") at the time he turned professional in 2015.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-lbsu-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-sdsu_record-20)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-22)
## Professional career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Professional career")]
### Web.com Tour
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Web.com Tour")]
After turning professional in June 2015, Schauffele entered the 2015 [Web.com Tour Qualifying Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web.com_Tour_Qualifying_Tournament "Web.com Tour Qualifying Tournament") in fall. He was runner-up in first stage at Southern Dunes GC in [Maricopa, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maricopa,_Arizona "Maricopa, Arizona"). He went on to win second stage at Oak Valley GC in [Beaumont, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaumont,_California "Beaumont, California"), and ultimately, narrowly, earned his [Web.com Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web.com_Tour "Web.com Tour") card in the finals in Florida in a tie for 45th.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-24)
In 2016, Schauffele played a full season (23 events) on the [Web.com Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web.com_Tour "Web.com Tour"). He finished 26th on the regular-season money list, missing a [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour") card for 2017 by less than $1,000, but went on to earn a card through the [Web.com Tour Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web.com_Tour_Finals "Web.com Tour Finals") by finishing 15th on the Finals money list (excluding the 25 regular-season graduates).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-25)
### 2016–17 PGA Tour: Rookie of the Year
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–17 PGA Tour: Rookie of the Year")]
Schauffele made his PGA Tour debut at the [CareerBuilder Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CareerBuilder_Challenge "CareerBuilder Challenge") in [La Quinta, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Quinta,_California "La Quinta, California"). In June 2017, at the [2017 U.S. Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_U.S._Open_\(golf\) "2017 U.S. Open \(golf\)") held at [Erin Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Hills "Erin Hills"), Schauffele recorded a bogey-free 6-under-par 66, the first time a player has returned a bogey-free round of 66 or better in their first appearance in [U.S. Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Open_\(golf\) "U.S. Open \(golf\)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-26) He subsequently became one of only 15 players to ever reach 10 under par at a U.S. Open.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-U.S._Open_Recap-27) He eventually finished in a tie for fifth place, earning him an exemption into the [2018 championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_U.S._Open_\(golf\) "2018 U.S. Open \(golf\)").
Three weeks later, in July, Schauffele recorded his first PGA Tour victory, at the [Greenbrier Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenbrier_Classic "Greenbrier Classic"). With the win, he earned exemptions into the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Open_Championship "2017 Open Championship"), via the Open Qualifying Series, the [PGA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_PGA_Championship "2017 PGA Championship") and the [2018 Masters Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Masters_Tournament "2018 Masters Tournament").
Schauffele qualified for the end-of-season [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship") by moving up to 26th in the standings, from 33rd at the start of the [FedEx Cup Playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_FedEx_Cup_Playoffs "2017 FedEx Cup Playoffs").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-28) There he birdied the 72nd hole to claim his second tour victory, by one stroke over [Justin Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Thomas "Justin Thomas"), and become the first rookie to win the Tour Championship. It was also the first time a rookie had won any FedEx Cup playoff event.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-29) The win moved Schauffele to third place in the final FedEx Cup standings, bettering the previous best mark by a rookie held by [Jordan Spieth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Spieth "Jordan Spieth") by four positions, and gave him a three-year exemption on the PGA Tour, through the 2019–20 season.
During 2017, Schauffele rose to 32nd in the [Official World Golf Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_World_Golf_Ranking "Official World Golf Ranking"), up 267 spots from his 2016 year-end position of 299. He was voted Rookie of the Year for 2017 by his peers.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-30)
### Continued success: 2018 season through 2024 season
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Continued success: 2018 season through 2024 season")]
At the beginning of 2018, Schauffele switched equipment manufacturers, signing an endorsement deal with [Callaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callaway_Golf_Company "Callaway Golf Company"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-31) having previously been sponsored by [TaylorMade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TaylorMade "TaylorMade").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-32) In May, he finished T2 at the [2018 Players Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Players_Championship "2018 Players Championship") at [TPC Sawgrass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPC_Sawgrass "TPC Sawgrass") with a score of 14 under par.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-33) In the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Open_Championship "2018 Open Championship") at [Carnoustie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnoustie_Golf_Links "Carnoustie Golf Links"), he tied for second with a score of 6 under par.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-34)
Schauffele began the [2018 FedEx Cup Playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FedEx_Cup_Playoffs "2018 FedEx Cup Playoffs") in 28th position in the standings. Entering the third of four events in the playoff series, the [2018 BMW Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Championship_\(PGA_Tour\) "BMW Championship \(PGA Tour\)"), he was 41st, needing to move up at least eleven spots to advance to the [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship"). He finished in a tie for third to rise to 18th position. That finish allowed him the opportunity to attempt to defend his 2017 Tour Championship title.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-35) Schauffele ultimately finished T7 at the 2018 Tour Championship, while placing 15th in the season-long [FedEx Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx_Cup "FedEx Cup").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-2018_FedExCup_Standings-36)
Schauffele joined the [2018 European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_European_Tour "2018 European Tour") as an associate member. With his win at the 2018 [WGC-HSBC Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGC-HSBC_Champions "WGC-HSBC Champions"), Schauffele rose in the [European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour "European Tour")'s Order of Merit, the year-long points race dubbed the [European Tour Race to Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour_Race_to_Dubai "European Tour Race to Dubai"), to 4th position.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-37) Schauffele entered the European Tour final event, the [DP World Tour Championship, Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DP_World_Tour_Championship,_Dubai "DP World Tour Championship, Dubai"), in 5th position. With a final round score of 6-under-par 66, which equaled the lowest score of the day, Schauffele finished T16. This ensured a season-ending 4th position on the Order of Merit and participation in the 2018 European Tour's bonus pool.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-38)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Xander_Schauffele_2020_Farmers_Open.jpg/250px-Xander_Schauffele_2020_Farmers_Open.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Xander_Schauffele_2020_Farmers_Open.jpg)Schauffele at the 2020 [Farmers Insurance Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers_Insurance_Open "Farmers Insurance Open")
In October 2018, Schauffele won the [WGC-HSBC Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGC-HSBC_Champions "WGC-HSBC Champions") event in [Shanghai, China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai,_China "Shanghai, China"), at the [Sheshan Golf Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheshan_Golf_Club "Sheshan Golf Club"), in a playoff, defeating [Tony Finau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Finau "Tony Finau") on the first extra hole.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-39) In January 2019, he won the [Sentry Tournament of Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentry_Tournament_of_Champions "Sentry Tournament of Champions") at The Plantation Course at [Kapalua Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapalua_Resort "Kapalua Resort") in [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui "Maui"), [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-40) returning a course record equalling 11-under-par 62 in the final round to pass [Gary Woodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Woodland "Gary Woodland"), whom he had trailed by five shots entering the final round.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-41)
In April, Schauffele tied for second in the [Masters Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Masters_Tournament "2019 Masters Tournament"), one stroke behind champion [Tiger Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Woods "Tiger Woods"). It was his third top-five in eight starts at major championships. He led the field with 25 birdies, becoming the third player since 1980 to have 25 or more birdies in a single Masters, joining [Phil Mickelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Mickelson "Phil Mickelson") (25 in 2001) and [Jordan Spieth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Spieth "Jordan Spieth") (28 in 2015).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-42) In June, he finished tied for 3rd at the [U.S. Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Open_\(golf\) "U.S. Open \(golf\)") at [Pebble Beach Golf Links](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pebble_Beach_Golf_Links "Pebble Beach Golf Links") in Pebble Beach, California.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-43) At [The Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Open_Championship "2019 Open Championship") in July 2019, he became the first player to have their [driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driver_\(golf\) "Driver \(golf\)") fail [The R&A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_R&A "The R&A")'s conformity test.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-44)
In early August 2019, Schauffele placed 4th in the inaugural 2019 [Wyndham Rewards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyndham_Rewards "Wyndham Rewards") Top 10.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-45) Through the playoffs, he fell to 8th in the standings entering the [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship"); this gave him a 6-shot deficit to the leader, [Justin Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Thomas "Justin Thomas"), under the new handicapping system. He had erased the deficit after the first round with a score of 6-under-par 64 and was tied for the lead going into the second round.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-46) He ultimately finished in second place, but took maximum world ranking points having returned the lowest aggregate score.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-47)
In December 2019, Schauffele played on the U.S. team at the [2019 Presidents Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Presidents_Cup "2019 Presidents Cup") at [Royal Melbourne Golf Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Melbourne_Golf_Club "Royal Melbourne Golf Club") in Australia. The U.S. team won 16–14. Schauffele went 3–2–0 and won his Sunday singles match against International team star and veteran [Adam Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Scott_\(golfer\) "Adam Scott \(golfer\)"). _[Golf Digest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_Digest "Golf Digest")_ called Schauffele the "unsung hero" of the U.S. team.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-48)
At the 16th tee of the final round of the [2021 Masters Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Masters_Tournament "2021 Masters Tournament"), Schauffele was in second place, two strokes behind the leader. However, at that hole, he shot a triple bogey, and ultimately finished third.
In August, Schauffele recorded a final-round of 67 to win the [Olympic gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_individual "Golf at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's individual"); he made an up-and-down for par on the final hole to beat Slovak [Rory Sabbatini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Sabbatini "Rory Sabbatini") by one shot.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-49) With the accomplishment, Schauffele became the first American since 1904 to win an Olympic gold medal in golf.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-50) In September, Schauffele played on the U.S. team in the [2021 Ryder Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ryder_Cup "2021 Ryder Cup") at [Whistling Straits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistling_Straits "Whistling Straits") in [Kohler, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohler,_Wisconsin "Kohler, Wisconsin"). The U.S. team won 19–9 and Schauffele went 3–1–0, winning in both fourball and foursomes, then losing his Sunday singles match against [Rory McIlroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_McIlroy "Rory McIlroy").
In April, Schauffele won the [Zurich Classic of New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich_Classic_of_New_Orleans "Zurich Classic of New Orleans"), a team event, with playing partner [Patrick Cantlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Cantlay "Patrick Cantlay"). In June, he won the [Travelers Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travelers_Championship "Travelers Championship") for his sixth PGA Tour victory.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-51) In July, he won the J. P. McManus Pro-Am, an unofficial event on the [European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour "European Tour") held at [Adare Manor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adare_Manor "Adare Manor"), after shooting a course record 64 in the first round.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-52) The same week, he won the co-sanctioned [Genesis Scottish Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis_Scottish_Open "Genesis Scottish Open") played at the [Renaissance Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Club "Renaissance Club") in [East Lothian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Lothian "East Lothian"), Scotland. It was his third PGA Tour victory in the 2021–22 season, and his seventh overall.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-53)
Schauffele qualified for the U.S. team at the [2022 Presidents Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Presidents_Cup "2022 Presidents Cup"); he won three and lost one of the four matches he played.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-54)
In September 2023, Schauffele played on the U.S. team in the [2023 Ryder Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Ryder_Cup "2023 Ryder Cup") at [Marco Simone Golf and Country Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Simone_Golf_and_Country_Club "Marco Simone Golf and Country Club") in [Guidonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guidonia_Montecelio "Guidonia Montecelio"), [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy. The European team won 16.5–11.5 and Schauffele went 1–3–0, including a win in his Sunday singles match against [Nicolai Højgaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolai_H%C3%B8jgaard "Nicolai Højgaard").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-55)
### 2024: Major championship wins
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2024: Major championship wins")]
Having only previously worked with his dad, Stefan, from the very beginning, Xander made a coaching change and started working with Chris Como for the 2024 season.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-q810-56)
In May 2024, Schauffele won his first major with a birdie on the final hole in the [PGA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_PGA_Championship "2024 PGA Championship") at [Valhalla Golf Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valhalla_Golf_Club "Valhalla Golf Club").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-57) Schauffele won the tournament with a score of 21 under par, which is a record low for a major championship.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-tsn-58) He beat [Bryson DeChambeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryson_DeChambeau "Bryson DeChambeau") by one stroke after DeChambeau also birdied the final hole.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-59)
In July, Schauffele won the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Open_Championship "2024 Open Championship") at [Royal Troon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Troon_Golf_Club "Royal Troon Golf Club"), the second major of his career. Schauffele became the first golfer to win two majors in one season when shooting a final-round 65 at each one.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-60) He also became the first golfer to win multiple majors in the same year since [Brooks Koepka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooks_Koepka "Brooks Koepka") won the 2018 U.S. Open and PGA Championship.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-61) Schauffele pulled away from a crowded leaderboard with a 31 on the back nine in the final round to beat [Justin Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Rose "Justin Rose") and [Billy Horschel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Horschel "Billy Horschel") by two shots.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-62)
In October 2025, Schauffele won the [Baycurrent Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baycurrent_Classic "Baycurrent Classic") in Japan for his first win of the year.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-63) Prior to the win, Schauffele had two top-10 finishes in the 2025 season, but failed to make the Tour Championship for the first time since 2017.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-64)

Schauffele is an enthusiastic cigar smoker.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-67) His father introduced him to cigars at the age of 10, and his favorite cigar is the [Montecristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montecristo_\(cigar\) "Montecristo \(cigar\)") No. 2.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-68) He has been featured by _[Cigar Aficionado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigar_Aficionado "Cigar Aficionado")_.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-69)
